name: Medina of Tunis
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1979.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Under the Almohads and the Hafsids, from the 12th to the 16th century, Tunis was considered one of the greatest and wealthiest cities in the Islamic world. Some 700 monuments, including palaces, mosques, mausoleums, madrasas and fountains, testify to this remarkable past.”
The Medina of Tunis has been a World Heritage Site since 1979 and contains some 700 monuments, including palaces, mosques, mausoleums, madrasas and fountains, according to Wikipedia.

The article says it was founded in 698 around the original core of the Zitouna Mosque and took its essential form in the Hafsid period, when Tunis became a religious, intellectual and economic centre.
